title: Panel Tilt
summary: Bolt a solar panel in along a × b, then find the unknown support that gives the panel a set area, or makes the supports parallel.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 10.6.3, Vector or cross product of two vectors
concepts: Right-hand rule and a × b = −b × a
Area of a parallelogram as |a × b|
A vector square to two given vectors
learningOutcome: The student can compute a cross product from components, use its direction and length, find an unknown component from a given area, and use a × b = 0 for parallel vectors.

levels.title: The mount bolt
levels.adds: Baseline: a × b is square to both a and b, points by the right-hand rule and has length |a||b| sin θ (Ex 10.4 Q1, Q2, Q6; Examples 22, 23).
hints: Use the determinant pattern with i, j and k on the top row.
Check that the bolt dotted with a and with b gives 0.
Swapping a and b flips every sign.

levels.title: The roof allows an area
levels.adds: New: the area of the parallelogram on a and b is |a × b|, so an unknown component gives an equation (Ex 10.4 Q9, Q10, Q12; Examples 24, 25).
hints: Put c into b and find a × b in terms of c.
Take the length: √(sum of the squares of the three parts).
Set it equal to the area wanted and solve for c.

levels.title: Folded flat
levels.adds: New: two vectors are parallel exactly when a × b = 0, so b is a multiple of a (Ex 10.4 Q5; Example 21; Misc Q12).
hints: If b is a multiple of a, the cross product is the zero vector.
Compare the known components of b with those of a to find the multiple.
Use that multiple on the first component to get c.

misconceptions: a × b is the same as b × a
The cross product of two vectors is a number
Parallel vectors have a cross product of 1
